function.description: Read your token balances on every chain Vex can reach: Khalani-covered EVM chains via Khalani, plus Solana and local chains like Robinhood Chain (4663) read direct from RPC. Defaults to your personal wallets, EVM (`eip155`) and Solana, in one call; pass `walletFamily`/`chainIds` only to narrow the scan. Use this when the user asks what they hold or what a position is worth, and after a swap, bridge or transfer to confirm the tokens landed: this reads live balances, `AgentScan` recorded history. Each row carries `balanceRaw` (atomic units, a DECIMAL string) beside `balance`, the SAME holding as a full-precision human amount - read `balance`, never divide `balanceRaw` yourself. `valueUsd` is a DISPLAY-GRADE ESTIMATE, never for sizing a trade: size from `balanceRaw` and `decimals`. A row with no usable price carries `valueUsd: null` with `priceUnavailable: true`, never a `0`; a row that could not be converted keeps its identity and `balanceRaw`, reports `balance: null` and names the cause in `unprojectableReason` - never dropped, decimals never guessed. On Solana, native SOL and wSOL share the same Jupiter route/pricing mint but NEVER a balance or spendability domain. Only `assetKind: native` identifies account SOL and only that account balance can pay network fees; `assetKind: spl` is wSOL and every other token account. Nothing unread vanishes: chainErrors, tokenErrors, accountErrors and `rejectedEntries` report it. TWO INDEPENDENT completeness axes travel on every snapshot AND the envelope, and one being false never implies the other: `inventoryComplete` says every holding was enumerated and read, `valuationComplete` that every known held row carries a value; `inventoryIncompleteReason` names the worst cause and `failedChainIds` the chains whose holdings are UNKNOWN, never zero. `truncated` and `truncationNote` say when rows were left out and how to widen the read; `tokenCount` and `totalUsd` describe the FULL scan. The field-by-field list is this tool's `returns`, served whole by vex_ToolDescribe.
function.name: WalletBalances

chainIds.description: Optional. Omit (or pass empty) to scan all supported chains (Khalani + local). To restrict, pass chain IDs/aliases either comma-separated ('ethereum,base,solana') or as an array (['ethereum','base']).

limit.description: Optional. Caps the PRICED non-native rows per wallet snapshot, top-N by held USD value. The structural native SOL row and held tokens with no usable price are appended outside this limit; unpriced held tokens are marked `priceUnavailable` and capped at 20 with the surplus counted in `unpricedOmitted`. Only applied when response_format='concise'; ignored under the default 'detailed'. `tokenCount`/`totalUsd` always reflect the full scan.

response_format.description: Response shape, 'concise' or 'detailed'. Default 'detailed'. 'detailed' returns every token per wallet; 'concise' is what enables the `limit` trim (top rows by held USD value) and sets `truncated` when rows were left out.

walletFamily.description: Which wallet FAMILY to read - 'eip155', 'solana', or 'all'. Default 'all' aggregates your EVM + Solana wallets. This is a wallet family, not a chain: chains go in `chainIds`.
